prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1463; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured was changing lanes. Police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. The driver is named on the policy, and nothing suggests the damage happened before coverage began.

Entry 2: Photos of the vehicle show damage that matches the described impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 3: Claimant reports neck and back strain consistent with the force of the collision. The injury pattern fits the kind of impact described. No earlier injury to the same body areas is known from prior records.

Entry 4: Photos confirm some details of the scene, but no independent witnesses have come forward. Claimant has given the same account of events in every conversation so far.

Entry 5: Treatment has grown to many times the usual amount for this type of injury, with near-daily visits. New body areas were added to the treatment plan several weeks after the crash. Requested additional records from the treating providers.

Entry 6: Reviewed the file with the claim team. The treatment pattern and timing will be evaluated against the injury description and the medical records before any settlement discussion with counsel.
